text:
alex_g: heads up — we've seen a burst of NV faults on us-west2-a10 yesterday evening, triaging now

maria_p: saw that, any pattern on op types or tenants?

alex_g: quick summary: spikes in `Xid 13` and `Xid 79` across a handful of pods. latency didn't spike much but requests dropped for some tenanted embedder jobs.

kevin_s: are those the same nodes that had ECC counters rising last week?

alex_g: partially overlap. I mapped the GPU serials -> tenant traces. three nodes (rack2b-4{1,2,3}) show both ECC increments and Xid 79 cluster-wide in the 22:00-23:30 window.

maria_p: payloads during the window: mostly long-context batching (seq_len > 1024) coming from dedicated embedder tenants + a couple of retriever workloads.

alex_g: logs from one host (snip):
```
[2026-03-17T22:14:02Z] nv_gpu: Xid 79: ECC single-bit error, kernel kill disabled
[2026-03-17T22:14:03Z] worker: decode loop abort, fallback to smaller batch
[2026-03-17T22:14:07Z] nv_gpu: Xid 13: illegal memory access during decode
```

kevin_s: interesting — Xid 79 often shows ECC/single-bit issues, Xid 13 suggests illegal access (driver/kernel/kernel-module mismatch or bad userspace). Could be memory pressure + degraded card.

maria_p: tenants running quantized int8 on a10s? We pushed an int8 patch yesterday to prod embedders.

alex_g: yes, two tenant fleets switched to the new quant profile at 21:50. rollout looked ok in canaries.

ops-bot: deployment event: tenant-embedder-v2 rolled to 30% at 2026-03-17T21:51:12Z; rolled to 100% at 2026-03-17T22:05:03Z

kevin_s: that timing aligns. Hypothesis: new int8 kernel exposed latent ECC-prone cards under long-sequence workloads causing memory-correctable errors -> Xid 79 -> subsequent illegal accesses (Xid 13) when retry paths hit bad cache state.

maria_p: can we correlate by kernel/driver versions? Use `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg` from impacted hosts.

alex_g: pulled those: drivers are uniform (525.105), but one host has bios microcode older than others. Also saw frequent soft ECC corrections on the three GPUs.

kevin_s: action plan suggestion:
- revert quant profile for affected tenant to previous int8 runtime (rollback flag)
- cordon + drain the three nodes, run memory/floating-point stress + ECC stress tests
- exchange cards if persistent or if single-bit ECC rate > threshold
- add runtime guard: detect repeated Xid 79 within 5m -> automatically fall back to safer kernel/quantization

maria_p: agree. also add a histogram of optype vs Xid code in observability so we can catch model/sequence correlations earlier.

alex_g: started rollback of tenant-embedder-v2 to 20% at 22:45. infra-bot reports rollback success to 100% by 22:52.

infra-bot: node actions queued: cordon rack2b-41, rack2b-42, rack2b-43; starting graceful drain.

kevin_s: while draining, capture `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` every 30s and upload to /shared/triage/1968456789/ so we can plot correctable error rate trends.

maria_p: I'll update the Optimize runbook: include quick checklist for quant rollout — preflight ECC baseline + progressive seq_len stress on canaries.

alex_g: one more datapoint: two other hosts reported Xid 48 earlier that day but those were unrelated (OOM in a custom kernel extension). We should keep code -> Xid mapping in our triage doc.

kevin_s: let's also tag the tenant in billing/alerts so we can throttle by tenant if the fallback isn't enough. Cost vs reliability tradeoff.

maria_p: agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket with steps and owners. short notes: rollback done, nodes draining, stress test scheduled 1h after drain completes, escalation to hardware swap if ECC > 1e3 correctable errors/hour.

alex_g: thanks — will watch for new Xids after rollback. please ping if you see reappears. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: triage-ticket created: INFRA-3729 — "NV fault cohort triage: A10 ECC/Xid spike us-west2" assigned to eng-infra oncall

kevin_s: marking this thread for postmortem if we end up replacing hardware.

alex_g: closing monitoring loop for now, keeping watch.
